 Medium

 Print PM Modi and DKS launched the mtero and also took a ride Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday inaugurated the Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere. The new stretch, developed at a cost of around Rs 3,470 crore, is expected to improve connectivity, ease daily commuting and reduce travel time for passengers. The elevated section will connect six stations: Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIMB (Bilekahalli-IIMB), JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere. Its opening will take Bengaluru's operational Metro network beyond 100 km for the first time. The Prime minister also took a ride before inaguration. Watch LIVE: PM Modi undertakes a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station Bengaluru Metro Pink Line : Route and stations
 The new stretch will run from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere in Bengaluru, covering six stations: Kalena Agrahara
 Hulimavu
 IIMB (Bilekahalli-IIMB)
 JP Nagar 4th Phase
 Jayadeva Hospital
 Tavarekere
 The corridor is expected to strengthen public transport connectivity in the city and make daily travel easier for commuters along the route. Project cost
 The Pink Line stretch from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere has been developed at a cost of around Rs 3,470 crore, according to the Prime Minister's Office. The project is part of a larger set of development works worth over Rs 15,600 crore that Modi is scheduled to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation or lay the foundation stone for during his Bengaluru visit. These projects cover urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways. The elevated stretch is part of the larger Pink Line project. The underground section is targeted for completion in 2027, according to the ANI report. The full corridor is expected to further expand Metro connectivity across Bengaluru. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also flagged off the new Yesvantpur-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express, connecting Bengaluru with coastal Karnataka and Goa. The service will provide direct connectivity to key destinations including Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Mangaluru, Udupi, Kundapura, Murdeshwar, Gokarna and Karwar. Join conversation

 The new chair car service is aimed at strengthening rail connectivity between Bengaluru, coastal Karnataka and Goa, while offering passengers a faster and more comfortable journey through the region's scenic landscapes. According to South Western Railway, regular operations will begin on November 15, following two inaugural special services on November 13. The PM had earlier laid the foundation stone of the Golden Jubilee Administrative Block and launch the S-VYASA off-campus in Thiruvananthapuram. Later, he will travel to Mysuru to inaugurate the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium.
